tabs.title: EKS: IRSA
tabs.summary: No keys: kubesentry's service account assumes an IAM role through the cluster's OIDC provider, and reaches Bedrock through a VPC endpoint.

steps.title: Enable model access
steps.text: In the Amazon Bedrock console of us-west-2, open Model access and request Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 (us.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5). The refusal fallback uses us.anthropic.claude-opus-5: request it too, or set the fallback to off. The first Anthropic model in an account also asks for the use-case form.

steps.title: Find the cluster's network
steps.text: The VPC, the private subnets of the nodes and the cluster security group.
steps.code:
aws eks describe-cluster --name prod-eks --region us-west-2 \
  --query 'cluster.resourcesVpcConfig.{vpc:vpcId,subnets:subnetIds,clusterSG:clusterSecurityGroupId}'

steps.title: Endpoint security group
steps.text: Allow HTTPS (TCP 443) into the endpoint from the nodes (or from the pods' security group with security groups for pods).
steps.code:
aws ec2 create-security-group --region us-west-2 --vpc-id <VPC_ID> \
  --group-name kubesentry-bedrock-endpoint --description 'Bedrock endpoint for kubesentry'
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --region us-west-2 --group-id <ENDPOINT_SG_ID> \
  --protocol tcp --port 443 --source-group <NODE_SG_ID>

steps.title: Endpoint policy
steps.text: Only kubesentry's role, only the inference action and the models. Save it as endpoint-policy.json.

steps.title: Create the interface VPC endpoint
steps.text: Service com.amazonaws.us-west-2.bedrock-runtime in the nodes' private subnets, with private DNS on: bedrock-runtime.us-west-2.amazonaws.com then resolves to private addresses inside the VPC, so no endpoint override is needed and no traffic leaves the VPC.
steps.code:
aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint --region us-west-2 --vpc-id <VPC_ID> \
  --vpc-endpoint-type Interface --service-name com.amazonaws.us-west-2.bedrock-runtime \
  --subnet-ids <PRIVATE_SUBNET_IDS> --security-group-ids <ENDPOINT_SG_ID> \
  --private-dns-enabled --policy-document file://endpoint-policy.json

steps.title: Role policy
steps.text: kubesentry's role needs bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream on the model and inference-profile ARNs (Bedrock API: runtime). Save it as investigator-policy.json.

steps.title: The cluster's OIDC issuer
steps.text: IRSA trusts the cluster's OIDC provider. The issuer is oidc.eks.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/id/EXAMPLED539D4633E53DE1B71EXAMPLE.

steps.title: Trust policy (IRSA)
steps.text: Only kubesentry's service account kubesentry/kubesentry may assume the role. Save it as trust-irsa.json.

steps.title: Create the role
steps.text: Create the role with the trust policy and attach the inference policy.
steps.code:
aws iam create-role --role-name kubesentry-investigator \
  --assume-role-policy-document file://trust-irsa.json
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name kubesentry-investigator --policy-name kubesentry-investigator \
  --policy-document file://investigator-policy.json

steps.title: Helm values
steps.text: Annotate kubesentry's service account with the role.
steps.code:
serviceAccount:
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::<ACCOUNT_ID>:role/kubesentry-investigator
incidents:
  enabled: true
  investigator:
    provider: bedrock
    bedrockAPI: runtime
    region: us-west-2
    # enabled: true and acknowledgeDataEgress: true here, or turn it on in Settings
    # settings: locked   # GitOps: Helm is the only source, the Settings page is read-only

steps.title: Test the connection
steps.text: Restart kubesentry so its pods pick up the role (kubectl -n kubesentry rollout restart deployment), then press Test connection above: it shows the role kubesentry runs as and sends a one-token request to the model. Turn the investigator on when it passes.

tabs.summary: No keys: an EKS Pod Identity association gives kubesentry's service account an IAM role; Bedrock through a VPC endpoint.

steps.title: Trust policy (Pod Identity)
steps.text: The EKS Pod Identity service assumes the role for the pod. Save it as trust-pod-identity.json.

steps.title: Create the role
steps.text: Create the role with the trust policy and attach the inference policy.
steps.code:
aws iam create-role --role-name kubesentry-investigator \
  --assume-role-policy-document file://trust-pod-identity.json
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name kubesentry-investigator --policy-name kubesentry-investigator \
  --policy-document file://investigator-policy.json

steps.title: Associate the role with kubesentry's service account
steps.text: Needs the Amazon EKS Pod Identity Agent add-on (and, in private clusters, the com.amazonaws.us-west-2.eks-auth endpoint). No annotation is needed.
steps.code:
aws eks create-pod-identity-association --region us-west-2 --cluster-name prod-eks \
  --namespace kubesentry --service-account kubesentry \
  --role-arn arn:aws:iam::<ACCOUNT_ID>:role/kubesentry-investigator

steps.title: Helm values
steps.text: Nothing to add for the role; point the investigator at Bedrock.
steps.code:
incidents:
  enabled: true
  investigator:
    provider: bedrock
    bedrockAPI: runtime
    region: us-west-2
    # enabled: true and acknowledgeDataEgress: true here, or turn it on in Settings
    # settings: locked   # GitOps: Helm is the only source, the Settings page is read-only

steps.title: Test the connection
steps.text: Restart kubesentry so its pods pick up the role (kubectl -n kubesentry rollout restart deployment), then press Test connection above: it shows the role kubesentry runs as and sends a one-token request to the model. Turn the investigator on when it passes.

tabs.title: Outside EKS
tabs.summary: From a laptop (remote mode) with your AWS profile or SSO sign-in, or in another cluster with a Kubernetes Secret the chart mounts.

steps.title: Enable model access
steps.text: In the Amazon Bedrock console of us-west-2, open Model access and request Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 (us.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5). The refusal fallback uses us.anthropic.claude-opus-5: request it too, or set the fallback to off. The first Anthropic model in an account also asks for the use-case form.

steps.title: Grant your identity the inference action
steps.text: From a laptop kubesentry calls Bedrock as you: add this statement to your IAM Identity Center permission set (or the role your profile assumes).

steps.title: Sign in with your AWS profile
steps.text: Remote mode reads the AWS profile like the AWS CLI does; with IAM Identity Center, sign in first. The session expires: sign in again when Test connection says the credentials expired.
steps.code:
aws sso login --profile <PROFILE>
export AWS_PROFILE=<PROFILE>

steps.title: Run kubesentry
steps.text: Remote mode, with incidents on; then turn the investigator on in Settings, or with flags.
steps.code:
kubesentry -kube-context <KUBE_CONTEXT> -incidents -aws-region us-west-2 \
  -investigator-bedrock-api runtime

steps.title: Other clusters: a Kubernetes Secret
steps.text: In a cluster outside AWS there is no pod role. Prefer short-lived credentials (IAM Roles Anywhere); otherwise put a dedicated, least-privilege user's keys in a Secret you manage and rotate. kubesentry never stores them: the chart mounts them as environment variables.
steps.code:
kubectl -n kubesentry create secret generic kubesentry-aws \
  --from-literal=AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="$AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID" \
  --from-literal=AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="$AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"

steps.title: Helm values for the Secret
steps.text: The server reads the keys from its environment.
steps.code:
extraEnv:
  - name: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
    valueFrom:
      secretKeyRef: {name: kubesentry-aws, key: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID}
  - name: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
    valueFrom:
      secretKeyRef: {name: kubesentry-aws, key: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}
incidents:
  enabled: true
  investigator:
    provider: bedrock
    bedrockAPI: runtime
    region: us-west-2
    # enabled: true and acknowledgeDataEgress: true here, or turn it on in Settings
    # settings: locked   # GitOps: Helm is the only source, the Settings page is read-only

steps.title: Test the connection
steps.text: Press Test connection above: it shows the identity kubesentry runs as and sends a one-token request to the model.

tabs.title: Anthropic API
tabs.summary: The alternative: Claude on the Anthropic API with an API key from a Kubernetes Secret.

steps.title: Create the Secret
steps.text: The key comes only from the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable, set from a Kubernetes Secret: kubesentry never stores it and the Settings page never takes it. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not set in this server's environment yet.
steps.code:
kubectl -n kubesentry create secret generic kubesentry-anthropic \
  --from-literal=api-key="$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"

steps.title: Helm values
steps.text: The chart sets ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from the Secret. Restart kubesentry after the first install of the Secret.
steps.code:
incidents:
  enabled: true
  investigator:
    provider: anthropic
    existingSecret: kubesentry-anthropic
    # apiKeyKey: api-key

steps.title: Network
steps.text: The pods need egress on 443 to api.anthropic.com (an egress proxy through HTTPS_PROXY in extraEnv works). Requests leave your network: the recommended setup is Bedrock through a VPC endpoint.

steps.title: Test the connection
steps.text: Choose the Anthropic API as the provider above, save, and press Test connection: a missing or wrong key answers 401.
